"Crowfall Founder’s Update

December - 2020

  1. What a crazy, eventful, memorable year.

When we closed the office back in March, Gordon and I were nervous. We had the capacity for people to work remotely -- but it was a convenience, something to give our team an occasional boost in flexibility when required. It certainly wasn’t intended to be used by our entire team -- all day, every day. Anyone who has worked with me also knows that, historically, I’ve never been a big fan of remote work.

But life happens, and you adapt. I’m pleased to say that it has worked, better than I expected. Harder in many ways, maybe even better in a few. I know that pretty much everyone had their life upended by COVID, though, so I won’t belabor the point. You guys know how crazy this year has been, and frankly, the fact that we were able to keep our team together -- and continue working on this project that we have put so much of our lives into -- is a blessing. I can’t complain.

Overall, in spite of the world exploding, 2020 has been a year of slow-and-steady progress for Crowfall. We completed our Series-A financing in January (thankfully -- lucky timing to have that behind us, going into March!). We successfully transitioned to the new normal in the spring, starting Alpha in May. Then in August we launched Beta. That month was our best since Kickstarter in terms of new registrations and new backers. It was the culmination of a deeper strategy game that included caravans, new conquest control points and strategy game features. All of these contributed to a higher level of player agency -- giving players more choices in how they choose to compete and greater empowerment in determining what path they take to victory in the Throne War. We’ve kept up a constant cadence of new versions, with our final features coming online, one-by-one. The list of things-we-need-to-launch grows smaller and smaller by the day. Client performance has steadily improved and we’re already to the point where our servers can handle the load we feel like we’ll need for launch.

I know there is work to be done. The game is not quite there, but it is close enough that I can see it now. Next year, when I write my End of 2021 Founder’s Update, it will be to discuss the game-that-is, not the game-that-will-be.

Coming into 2021, I am filled with excitement for what the new year holds for Crowfall, the ArtCraft team and for you, our player community. There are a handful of features that I’m excited about (like the Castle, the tournament system, the fps improvements from our work with Unity and, of course, getting a chance to finally do a balance pass -- which I’ve been wanting to do for a long time!). But beyond even that, I’m excited to see this game launch and become real. I’m excited to put our last “wipe” behind us and open the doors to new players who will be seeing our game for the first time. I’m excited for the backers who have been with us since the Hunger Dome days -- our first playable PvP test -- who will be able to say “I was there when it started,” and for those of you who joined us along the way. It is quite a thing, to witness the birth of an MMO from concept to completion. It is a messy and sometimes frustrating and altogether magical process—one that is normally only witnessed by the development team. Not this time. You’ve dreamed with us, laughed with us, played with us and worked with us to make it happen, to make it real. You helped us breathe life into this bold and audacious vision.

And we will always be thankful for it.

In closing, let me wish a heartfelt goodbye to 2020, and a grateful welcome to 2021. Thank you again for joining us on this adventure, and as always -- we will see you in game!

Sincerely,

Todd & Gordon and the ACE team"
Crowfall Founder's Update - December 2020 - J Todd Coleman
